The vector (P_i−P̄)_i sums to zero, and the linear barycentric map is an isomorphism onto the zero-sum space. The chosen shift makes every canonical first-order value P̄. The moving strip limit then contradicts the violation.

The volume-cap map for the fixed K_ε is continuous jointly in point and normal because every hyperplane is volume-null; minimization on the compact normal sphere preserves continuity in the point. A maximum exists on K_ε and is global by separation. Outside int T a cap has zero T-volume and added volume O(ε), so every maximizer lies in int T for small ε. Each canonical cap upper test then gives λ_i(y_ε)≤1/m+O(ε) via the positive d-th root near d/m; sum one supplies the matching lower bounds. At y_ε=g_T+O(ε) the average of the canonical caps cancels every linear center term and gives the matching upper bound.

The strip limit cap multiplicity on r=0 is N(s), with the −r coordinate identically zero. The raw derivative is (dV/m)∫Nψ; subtracting Γd∫ψ on normalization gives (d/m)E_d. The nonaffine denominator is positive to first order by continuity and full support, and the facet inequality gives exactly Γc. For affine ψ the two linear coefficients vanish, and for ψ≡0 both bodies coincide with T.

Independently verified the sharp example with ℓ=1/d and ψ=min s_i. Its mean is 1/d², |K_ε|=V(1+ε/d), and |S_ε|=V(1+ε/d)^d, so the exact missing fraction is 1−(1+ε/d)^(1−d). The moment ∫Nψ is d times the integral of Pr(s_1≥1/m,min s≥u); the survival polynomials are (1−1/m−(d−1)u)^(d−1) up to 1/m and (1−du)^(d−1) above. Their integral is Γ/(d−1)−(1/m)^d/[d(d−1)], giving the equality ratio Γc. Rational polynomial integration checked this for each 2≤d≤20 and gave depth derivative 1/27 for d=2.

The normalized density difference for the smaller and larger body is positive only in the smaller body, with positive mass 1−|K_ε|/|S_ε|; this is the supremum absolute probability discrepancy and bounds every closed-halfspace discrepancy.

overlap.comparison: The accepted ordinary simplex equality classification and compact gap supply orientation and the unperturbed equality values. They give no fixed-roof maximum-depth derivative, explicit enclosing simplex, or sharp first-order ratio.

The accepted ordinary Hausdorff stability assertion gives compactness and continuity for near-minimal depth after normalization. It provides no sharp linear coefficient. The current statement is pointwise for one fixed roof and displayed majorant; its little-o statement does not yield uniform stability for varying roofs or arbitrary bodies.

The accepted smooth support-bump result differentiates a finite cap-cover upper bound in a stationary smooth setting. It neither applies to a simplex roof nor establishes the all-normal matching lower bound, the enclosing-simplex volume, or the ratio here.

Its general first-variation theorem contains the raw maximum-depth expansion as a specialization, and also gives maximizer displacement. The frozen proof reproduces the derivative directly for the actual strip and adds the enclosing-simplex comparison, sharp ratio and total variation conclusion.
